section.sectionSummaryBrief: The deeds of the Forefathers are a sign for the children, empowering each Jew to serve G-d with revealed joy founded on self-nullification, which breaks boundaries and leads to supernal vitality and long life.
section.t: And the deeds of the Forefathers are a sign for the children,
that the service of Sarah is instruction and empowerment for every single Jew
[and even that this matter in every single Jew is
(like all matters of the Forefathers and Matriarchs)
by inheritance73],
so that he can serve G-d with joy in a revealed manner,
and the joy will be founded upon the matter of self-nullification,
and "Let my soul be as dust to all"74.
Therefore there is no concern75
that from this will branch off some undesirable matter, G-d forbid,
and on the contrary,
since joy breaks boundaries,
behold through joy he will increase strength in his service with greater excellence and greater vigor,
until service that is above measure and limitation,
the matter of the intensification of vitality in service.
And through this there is also an intensification of life in its simple sense,
length of days and good years in simplicity.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This connects to the Rebbe's 120th birthday, linking Moshe's drawing of life from the Tree of Life to the Rebbe and his son, who continue to intercede and draw blessings for all Israel.
section.t: And one should connect this with the birthday of the Rebbe, of blessed memory, of this year,
(conclusion and seal)
the one hundred and twentieth year76,
for it is stated in the Zohar77
on the verse78
"And his days shall be one hundred and twenty years," that it alludes to Moshe etc., who draws down life to the children of man
(to every single Jew)
from that Tree of Life,
which also includes length of days in simplicity,
and as it is stated in the Zohar there
(before this)
"Inasmuch as"78
"this is Moshe"79
etc. "and from this power, children of man endure in the world for many days."
And this matter Moshe draws down even now,
as the Zohar there states "Moshe did not die" etc.,
and our sages said80
"Just as there he stands and serves, so too here he stands and serves."
And as it is with Moshe Rabbeinu, the Faithful Shepherd,
so too is it with the shepherds of Israel in every generation,
including the one whose birthday it is and his son, the Rebbe, my master, father-in-law, who fills his place,
and as is known the letter of the Rebbe, my master, father-in-law81
(regarding his father.
And from this it is understood that it is also so with him82)
that the shepherds of Israel will not be separated, G-d forbid, from the flock of their pasture,
which is in the manner of the aforementioned statement of our sages regarding Moshe, "Just as there he stands and serves, so too here he stands and serves,"
that even now he
(the one whose birthday it is,
and consequently it is understood—his son who fills his place)
pleads merit for each and every one of Israel,
and draws down for them blessings, successes, and salvations,
and even draws from the aspect of the Tree of Life
(the Tree of Life)
and also length of days in simplicity for each and every one of Israel.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Just as Sarah's life prefigures the future "we shall live before Him," so too the empowerment for joyful service leads to the revelation of the third day—the Third Temple—through joy that breaks boundaries, exemplified by King David's self-nullification.
section.t: And behold, just as the matter of "her life was life"
(of Sarah)
is analogous to "we shall live before Him" that will be in the future
(as above at the end of section 4 and section 5 of the maamar of the one whose birthday it is),
so too is it regarding the matter of the empowerment that is drawn from this for every Jew for service with joy
(as above in section 8),
that through service with joy we will merit in the very near future the fulfillment of the prophecy52
"On the third day He will raise us up and we shall live before Him."
And the explanation is,
behold it is explained in Likkutei Torah
(the discourse "He will revive us after two days, on the third day He will raise us up and we shall live before Him"83),
that the two days are the aspects of the One Who Fills All Worlds and the One Who Encompasses All Worlds,
and "on the third day" is the aspect that is above even the aspect of the One Who Encompasses All Worlds.
That is to say, that there is in it no measurements or limitations,
not even the measurement of the One Who Encompasses All Worlds.
And since joy breaks boundaries,
and through joy one reaches
(as above in section 8)
service that is above measure and limitation,
therefore joy
(in the service of G-d)
is a close preparation and vessel for the revelation of the aspect of "on the third day"
("He will raise us up and we shall live before Him"),
the aspect that is above
(also)
the aspect of the One Who Encompasses All Worlds,
which revelation will be in the Third Holy Temple,
and as the interpretation84
that "on the third day" refers to the Third Holy Temple,
which will be built by King Moshiach85,
a king from the House of Dovid86.
And also this matter is particularly connected to the matter of joy,
as is understood from the fact that the Rambam87
brings a proof for the matter of joy—that a person should rejoice
(every person)
in the performance of a mitzvah—from Dovid, king of Israel, about whom it is written88
"And the king89
Dovid was leaping and dancing before the L-rd" etc.
And one can explain this,
that Dovid, king of Israel, is the matter of the Sefirah of Malchus90,
and this is that he was in ultimate self-nullification,
"If I did not set [my soul] in stillness and silence"91,
for Malchus is an aspect of self-nullification,
as above
(section 4).
And this is that his service was with great joy,
and "the king Dovid was leaping and dancing before the L-rd,"
for from the perspective of the self-nullification of Malchus, even when joy is in a revealed manner, it is not possible that an undesirable matter will branch off from it.
And since Dovid, king of Israel, lives and endures92,
meaning that he lives and endures
(in every single Jew)
as Dovid, king of Israel
(the self-nullification of Malchus),
therefore he gives the power to every Jew to rejoice in the performance of a mitzvah
(even though it is a great service93),
and that the joy will be in a desirable manner.
